Free tools · Instant answers

Small tools, big daily help

No app to install, nothing to save. Type your numbers and get your answer right here.

Is my weight healthy?

BMI (Body Mass Index) is a quick first check used by doctors worldwide. It is a guide, not a diagnosis — muscle, age and body type also matter.

Your result will appear here.

How much water should I drink?

A common guide is about 35 ml of water per kg of body weight each day — more when it is hot or you exercise. Sip through the day instead of drinking it all at once.

Your result will appear here.

The 50 · 30 · 20 budget

A simple rule used all over the world: 50% of income for needs, 30% for wants, 20% for savings. Enter your monthly income in any currency.

Your split will appear here.

25-minute focus timer

The Pomodoro method: focus on one task for 25 minutes, then rest for 5. It works for study, office work and housework alike.

The 2-minute rule

If a task takes less than 2 minutes, do it now — don't write it down.

Reply to that message, hang that shirt, wash that one glass. Small things done instantly never pile up.

Daily routines

A day that runs itself

You don't need a perfect routine — just the same few good steps, in the same order, most days.

Morning · Subah

Wake up right in 30 minutes

  1. 1
    Water firstOne full glass before tea or coffee.
  2. 2
    Sunlight & movementOpen the curtains, stretch or walk for 5 minutes.
  3. 3
    Make your bedYour first finished task of the day.
  4. 4
    Pick 3 prioritiesWrite just three things that matter today.
  5. 5
    Eat a real breakfastProtein + fruit keeps energy steady till lunch.

Evening · Shaam

Wind down & sleep deep

  1. 1
    10-minute tidyReset the room so tomorrow starts clean.
  2. 2
    Prepare tomorrowClothes, bag and keys in one place.
  3. 3
    Screens downDim lights and put the phone away 30 minutes before bed.
  4. 4
    Note one good thingOne line about today — gratitude calms the mind.
  5. 5
    Same time, every nightA fixed sleep time beats a long lie-in.

Emergency help

Numbers that work almost anywhere

In a real emergency, call first — don't search. Save your local number in your phone today.

112

Most of the world

Works across Europe, India and many other countries — and on most phones even without a SIM.

911

USA & Canada

Police, fire and ambulance across the United States, Canada and parts of Latin America.

999

UK & others

The emergency number for the United Kingdom and several Commonwealth countries.

000

Australia

Police, fire and ambulance anywhere in Australia. (Triple zero.)

First 60 seconds anywhere: stay calm → move to safety → call the number → say where you are first, then what happened → follow the operator's instructions and don't hang up until they say so.
